name: Serena Yeung-Levy
title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering and of Computer Science
lab_name: Medical AI and Computer Vision Lab (MARVL)
research_topics: virtual cell / cellular morphology generative modeling
3D human mesh recovery and human motion from video
current_direction: Generative 'virtual cell' models of cellular morphology (flow matching + RL)
Biomedical vision-language corpora and benchmarks mined from scientific literature
RL / test-time post-training for multimodal scientific reasoning and tool use
Efficiency and perception bottlenecks in small and accelerated multimodal models
Computer vision for surgical and clinical video (steps, errors, competencies)
current_direction_basis: Driven by the 2025-2026 items on https://marvl.stanford.edu/publications.html, cross-checked against OpenAlex works for author A5093429554. Virtual-cell direction: 'CellFluxV2: An Image Generative Foundation Model for Virtual Cell Modeling' (bioRxiv, Jan 2026), 'CellFluxRL: Biologically-Constrained Virtual Cell Modeling via Reinforcement Learning' (arXiv 2026), and 'CellFlux: Simulating Cellular Morphology Changes via Flow Matching' (ICML 2025). Biomedical VLM data/benchmarks: 'BIOMEDICA' (CVPR 2025), 'MicroVQA' (CVPR 2025), 'From Panel to Pixel' (CVPR 2026), 'No Tokens Wasted' (arXiv 2025). RL/test-time training and tool use: 'PaperSearchQA ... with RLVR' (EACL 2026), 'Tool Verification for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning' (arXiv 2026), 'TTRV: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for Vision Language Models' (arXiv 2025). Efficiency/perception limits: 'Feather the Throttle' (ICCV 2025), 'Downscaling Intelligence' (CVPR 2026), 'Do VLMs Perceive or Recall?' (CVPR 2026). Surgical/clinical video: 'Computer Vision-Based Retrieval of Steps and Errors in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy' (medRxiv Jan 2026; OpenAlex shows an npj Digital Surgery 2026 version), 'Automated Video-Based Analysis of Surgical Meta-competencies' (medRxiv 2025), 'Enhanced Trauma Video Review With Computer Vision' (Annals of Surgery Open 2025).

state_rationale: OPENING UPHELD after adversarial re-check on 2026-08-31. The recruiting URL on record (https://marvl.stanford.edu/) returned HTTP 200 and carries, under the heading 'Interested in Joining?', this literal sentence: 'We have openings on a rolling basis for postdocs, rotation PhD students (already accepted to Stanford), and a limited number of MS or advanced undergraduate students.' That satisfies both tests: it is present-tense open ('We have openings on a rolling basis') and it names undergraduates specifically rather than only routing prospective PhD applicants to the graduate admissions pipeline. Corroboration fetched in the same pass: a live 'Master/Undergraduate Students' section on the people page (Jeffrey Heo, Christopher Polzak), and Stanford Profiles listing her for 2025-26 'Supervised Undergraduate Research CS 195', 'Senior Project CS 191', 'CS 191W' and 'Independent Work CS 199'. The lab is unambiguously active: the publications page has a full 2026 section (CVPR 2026, EACL 2026, plus bioRxiv/medRxiv/arXiv preprints). FOUR CAVEATS THAT A STUDENT MUST SEE BEFORE APPLYING. (1) The statement is UNDATED and its freshness could not be tested - web.archive.org returned 503 / timed out on every attempt, so there is no way to tell from this task whether the sentence is current copy or long-standing boilerplate. (2) The stated undergraduate route is NOT email: the page sends postdocs and Stanford PhD students to Serena's inbox, but sends 'a current student in other degree programs at Stanford' to a Google interest form - and that form could not be reached (three curls returned http_code=000/size 0; one attempt returned only a Google 'You must sign in to access this content' interstitial), so it is unverified whether the actual application channel for undergrads still works. (3) It is scoped to people already at Stanford: 'For others not currently at Stanford, we apologize if we may not have the bandwidth to respond.' (4) The wording is hedged - 'a limited number' of 'advanced' undergraduates - and the lab news list has not been updated since Oct 2025, so the page is maintained unevenly. Confidence set to 0.72 rather than higher because the opening sentence is real and verbatim but undated, and the undergraduate application route behind it is unverifiable.
